hero.headline: Your move.
hero.sub: Chess, ludo, draughts and pool against real players across Africa. Start with {{tokens}} free tokens.
hero.posterAlt: A chess board in the middle of a game. The opponent’s knight has just moved and it is your turn.

games.title: Games to play online
games.sub: Chess, ludo, draughts and pool, with more on the way. One account and one wallet for every game on the hub.
games.chessBlurb: Blitz and rapid games against real opponents, paired by rating.
games.stakes: Play free, or stake {{min}} to {{max}} tokens
games.ludoBlurb: The classic race home, one against one. The dice are thrown by the server, so nobody can load them.
games.poolBlurb: 8-ball and 9-ball on a full table. Every shot is played out on the server, so the table you see is the table that counts.
games.draughtsBlurb: International draughts on a 10 by 10 board. Capturing is compulsory, and every move is checked by the server.
games.checkupBlurb: The shape-matching card game played across Nigeria, for two to four players. The cards are dealt on the server and your hand is never sent to anyone else.
games.wordsBlurb: The crossword board game for two to four players: make words with your tiles and outscore the table. Words are judged on the server and your tiles are never sent to anyone else.
games.owareBlurb: The sowing game of Ghana and the wider region, Abapa rules. Sow your seeds, take two or three at a time, and be the first to 25. Every move is checked by the server.
games.basketballBlurb: Half-court street basketball in 3D, one against one: dribble, cross over, and hit your jump shot at the right moment. Practice against the computer now; online matches are coming.

steps.title: Create an account
steps.body: A username, an email and your country. It takes a minute. You must be 18 or older.

steps.title: Get {{tokens}} free tokens
steps.body: They are in your wallet as soon as you confirm your email.

steps.title: Play real opponents
steps.body: Pick a stake and a time control. We pair you with a player near your rating, from anywhere in Africa.

steps.title: Win tokens
steps.body: The winner takes the pot, less a {{rake}}% fee. For now the hub is free to play: tokens have no cash value. Playing for real money, with deposits and cash-outs, is coming later and only in countries where it is licensed.

items.title: Every move is checked by the server.
items.body: Your phone only shows the game. It cannot make an illegal move or change the position.

items.title: The clocks run on the server.
items.body: Time is measured on our side, so nobody gains seconds by tampering with their device.

items.title: Your wallet records every token.
items.body: Each stake, win and refund is written to a ledger that cannot be edited afterwards.

countries.title: Online games across Africa
countries.sub: Players from {{count}} countries can sign up today.
countries.languages: The hub speaks English and French. Portuguese, Swahili, Arabic and Kinyarwanda are on the way.

footer.responsible: For adults only. Play for the game, set yourself limits, and stop when it stops being fun.

about.metaDescription: Who we are and why we built African Game Hub: one fair place to play chess, ludo, draughts, pool and more against real people across Africa.
about.title: Made in Africa, for players across Africa.
about.intro: African Game Hub is one place to play the games we grew up with, against real people, on any phone. Chess, ludo, draughts, pool, Check Up and Word Battle, with one account for all of them.

mission.title: Our mission
mission.body: To give every player in Africa a fair, fast and friendly place to compete in the games they love, and a rating that shows how good they really are.

items.title: Fair play, checked by our server
items.body: Every move is checked by our server, and the clocks are kept there too. Nobody can change the app to win.

items.title: Made for the phone in your hand
items.body: It runs in the browser, opens fast, and is light on data. It works on budget Android phones and slow connections, with a data-saver setting.

items.title: One account, every game
items.body: A rating for each game, leaderboards for all of Africa and for your own country, friends, chat, challenges and tournaments.

items.title: Skill comes first
items.body: Games you get better at by playing, against real people, with ratings that show it.

items.title: Free today, honest about tomorrow
items.body: Playing is free. Tokens are free play money with no cash value. Deposits and withdrawals will come later, country by country, only where we are licensed.

items.title: We protect your account
items.body: Sign-up needs only an email and a password. We never ask for your card details or your mobile money PIN, and every token movement is recorded.

items.title: For adults, played responsibly
items.body: The hub is for people aged 18 and over. Play for the game, set yourself limits, and stop when it stops being fun.

founder.title: Meet the founder
founder.body: Emmanuel George is a software engineer with a BSc degree and the founder of African Game Hub. Emmanuel designed and built the hub to bring the games played at home, in school yards and on the streets of Africa to one fair place online, where anyone with a phone can compete, climb the rankings and make new friends.

legal.draft: Draft. This text has not yet been reviewed by a lawyer.

sections.p: You must be 18 or older and may hold one account only. You are responsible for keeping your login details private.

Tokens are the unit used in every game on the hub. For now the hub is free to play: the tokens you are given and the tokens you win are free-play tokens. They have no cash value and cannot be bought, sold, transferred for money or withdrawn. Real-money deposits and withdrawals are switched off and will only be offered in countries where African Game Hub is licensed to do so. When they are, it will be with new balances: free-play tokens will not be converted into money.

When you join a staked match, your stake is held until the game ends. The winner receives the pot less the platform fee shown before the match. A drawn or aborted game returns each player’s stake in full.
Using a chess engine or outside help, playing against your own accounts, or arranging results is not allowed. We may close accounts and withhold tokens gained by cheating.
What happens to stakes and purchases when something goes wrong is set out in the Refund policy.
Be decent to other players. Abuse, threats, hate speech and spam in chat are not allowed. You can block and report a player; we may mute or close accounts that break this rule.
You may close your account at any time by writing to us. We may suspend or close an account that breaks these terms. Free tokens are lost when an account is closed.

We work to keep the hub running and fair, but games can be interrupted by faults or by lost connections. A game that cannot be finished because of a fault on our side is called off and every stake returned.
We may update these terms as the hub grows. We will tell you in the app before a change takes effect.

Your email address, username, country, language, a record of your games and token movements, your friends list, and the messages you send (private messages to friends, and chat during a match). A phone number will only be stored if you add one. We ask for nothing we do not need to run your account.

To run your account, pair you with opponents, keep an accurate wallet, keep players safe, and detect cheating. We rely on your agreement to the Terms of use when you create an account, and on our duty to keep the games fair.
Your username, country flag, games won or rating, and finished games. Never your email address, phone number or wallet.
We use no advertising or analytics trackers and embed nothing from other companies in our pages. We do not build a profile of you for marketing and we do not sell or rent your data.
To keep you signed in and remember your settings, the app saves a small amount of information in your browser. The Cookies policy lists exactly what.

sections.h: Who handles the data for us
sections.p: Your account and game data are held by our database provider (Supabase), and our pages are delivered by our web host (Amazon Web Services), which sees your internet address as any web host does. Sign-in emails are sent through our email provider. They act only on our instructions. When you sign up or log in, a security check provided by Cloudflare (Turnstile) tells people from automated programs. For that, Cloudflare sees your internet address and some details of your browser, and uses them only for this check.

For as long as your account is open. When an account is closed we delete or anonymise personal details within 90 days, except records of token movements and games, which we keep for as long as the law and fair-play investigations require.

Passwords are stored only in scrambled (hashed) form that we cannot read. All connections are encrypted. Each player can read only their own wallet and messages, and only our servers can change balances or games.
The hub is for adults. We do not knowingly keep data about anyone under 18; an account found to belong to a minor is closed and its details removed.

You can ask us for a copy of your data, to correct it, or to close your account and delete it, by writing to the contact address below. If you are unhappy with our answer you may complain to the data protection authority in your country.
If we change how we use your data we will update this page and tell you in the app before the change takes effect.
African Game Hub is about skill and competition. It is not a way to earn a living, and nobody should stake what they cannot afford to lose.
You must be 18 or older. Accounts found to belong to minors are closed.

Decide how much time and how many tokens you are willing to spend before you start, and stop when you reach that point. Limits, cool-off periods and self-exclusion will be available in your settings before real money is switched on anywhere.
Take a break, and talk to someone you trust. If you want your account paused or closed, write to the contact address on the home page.

legal.whoIntro: African Game Hub is run by the business below. Write to us about anything on this page.

sections.p: We set no advertising or tracking cookies, and no other company sets any through our pages. That is why you are not shown a cookie banner: there is nothing optional to accept or refuse. The security check on the sign-up and log-in pages is provided by Cloudflare. It sets no advertising or tracking cookies.

sections.h: What the app saves in your browser
sections.p: Three things, all needed for the app to work: your sign-in session, so you stay logged in; your settings, such as sound, board and language; and your last choices in the lobby. For offline use, the app also keeps a copy of its own files and of the last wallet and profile it showed you.
Logging out removes your session. Clearing this site’s data in your browser settings removes everything; you will simply need to log in again.
If we ever add anything that is not strictly needed, such as measuring visits, we will ask for your consent first and update this page.
At present the hub uses free play tokens with no cash value. Nothing can be bought, so there is nothing to refund.
A stake is returned in full, automatically, when a game is drawn, is called off before both players have played, or is cancelled by our team. A stake on a game you lost fairly is not returned.
If a fault on our side costs you tokens, write to us with the date and your username. Every token movement is recorded, so we can check it, and we will put right what was lost.

Deposits and withdrawals will only be switched on in countries where we are licensed. Before that happens, this page will set out how to ask for a refund of a deposit that has not been played, how long it takes, and any fees. Money lost in a fairly played game will not be refundable.
Where a game is found to have been won by cheating, we may reverse the result and return the stake to the player who was cheated.

rules.title: How to play
rules.men: This is international draughts, on a board of 10 by 10. White moves first. A man moves one square diagonally forward.
rules.capture: A man captures by jumping an enemy piece next to it, forward or backward, onto the empty square just behind. If it can jump again from there, it goes on.
rules.most: Capturing is compulsory, and you must play the capture that takes the most pieces. Captured pieces are lifted when the whole move is over, and none can be jumped twice.
rules.kings: A king moves any distance along a diagonal and captures from a distance, landing on any empty square behind the piece it takes.
rules.crown: A man becomes a king when its move ends on the far row. A man that only passes that row during a capture stays a man.
rules.win: You win when your opponent cannot move: no pieces left, or every piece blocked. Running out of time loses.
rules.draw: A draw: the same position three times; 25 moves each with kings only and no capture; or a lone king that is not caught in 16 moves each by three pieces, or in 5 moves each by one or two.

rules.title: How to play
rules.board: Oware (Abapa) is played on two rows of six pits, with four seeds in each: 48 seeds. Your row is the one nearest you. The first player moves first.
rules.sow: On your turn, pick one of your pits that has seeds. All its seeds are sown one by one into the pits that follow, going round the board anticlockwise.
rules.lap: A pit with twelve seeds or more goes all the way round the board: the pit it was emptied from is skipped.
rules.capture: If your last seed lands in an opponent’s pit and makes it two or three, you take those seeds, and the seeds of the pits just before it on their side, for as long as they also hold two or three.
rules.grandSlam: A move that would take every seed your opponent has is played, but takes nothing.
rules.feed: If your opponent’s row is empty, you must play a pit that gives them seeds, if you have one.
rules.win: The first to take 25 seeds wins. At 24 each the game is a draw. Running out of time loses.
rules.end: If an empty row cannot be fed, if the same position comes round three times, or after 100 moves without a capture, each player takes the seeds left in their own row, and the one with more wins.

rules.title: How to play
lines: Play a card of the same shape or the same number as the card on top. If you cannot, go to market: draw one card.
2, Pick two: the next player draws two, unless they play a 2 and pass it on.
5, Pick three: the next player draws three, unless they play a 5 and pass it on.
8, Suspension: the next player misses a turn.
14, General market: everyone else draws one, and you play again.
20: goes on any card. You call the shape the next player must play.
The first to play every card wins. If the market finishes first, the cards are counted and the lowest count wins. A star counts double; a 20 counts 20.
Let your turn run out and the game goes to market for you. Do it twice in a row and you are out.

computer.listFailed: The word list could not be fetched. Touch to try again.

rules.title: How to play
lines: Make words on the board with your seven tiles. Touch a tile, then the square it goes on. Touch a tile you have laid to take it back.
The first word must cover the star in the middle. Every word after it must join the tiles already down, and every word it makes, across and down, must be a real word.
Each tile scores the number on it. 2L and 3L double or triple the letter laid on them; 2W and 3W double or triple the whole word. A bonus square counts only on the turn it is covered.
Use all seven tiles in one turn for 50 extra points.
A blank tile stands for any letter and scores nothing.
Instead of playing you may swap tiles (while the bag holds at least seven) or pass.
The game ends when a player has no tiles left and the bag is empty, or when nobody has scored for two rounds. Tiles left on a rack are taken off that player’s score. The highest score wins.
Words are judged by an English word list. Let your turn run out and it is passed; do it twice in a row and you are out.
